document_title: 112 Answers in Palmer, and Where They Go
post_copy:
22 legislative candidates were in a Palmer theater on October 4th as the crowd answered a question on AI data centers.

57 of 112 chose "Outlaw them entirely." 47 chose strict regulations and 8 chose allow. That's a room with its tally on screen, not all of Mat-Su.

On Mat-Su land, the question's "state" is three rooms. DNR is deciding whether AIDEA gets about 19,950 acres near Houston. AIDEA lists data centers among possible uses and says none is proposed. The University of Alaska leased 829 acres at Port MacKenzie.

The third is the Legislature, where data center bill SB 250 passed the Senate 14 to 5 and stalled in a House committee. Early voting opens October 19th.

Pictured are the room's phones, the Houston land, the Port MacKenzie parcels, a gavel on SB 250 and the voting calendar.

Should only the Legislature set the rules for data centers on state land?

#MatSu #AIDEA #AKLeg

aftercare: Post Tuesday, October 13th or Wednesday, October 14th, 8 to 11 a.m. Alaska time, before early voting opens October 19th. Drafts arrive daily and the posting cadence is yours. Don't post this one on or after October 19th without updating slide 09's ask.
Paste the first comment (sources, the note on the room, the context invite and the site line) within 60 seconds of posting.
Reply to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes.

In replies, never call the forum a poll or survey of Mat-Su. It was a room answering on phones with the tally on screen. Never imply any candidate's position on data centers. Never say a data center is planned on the Houston land or that the Port MacKenzie lease is for data centers. SB 250 stalled in a House committee. Never say the House never took it up.
After 48 hours, note the saves, comments and reposts so the ledger can learn from them.
editor_notes_for_email: No.85 leads with the Mat-Su Sentinel's October 4th forum because it is a counted answer from a room that held 22 legislative candidates, set against the three bodies that actually decide data centers on Mat-Su land, a week before early voting. Every count is described as a room answering on phones with the tally on screen and never as a poll of Mat-Su, and nothing implies any candidate's view. AIDEA's Houston plan is said to list data centers among possible uses with AIDEA saying none is proposed, and the Port MacKenzie lease is never called a data center lease. The lessee rests on the Sentinel and university officials, because the university's own notice names none. SB 250 is written as stalled in a House committee per BASIS, and the AJOC piece is cited as 2026-09-28 even though its URL path reads 10/04.
